cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Geological hazards arise from Earth processes that pose risk to people and property: landslides, subsidence, earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, flooding

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Landslides (mass movement): rockfalls, slides, flows and creep; triggered by heavy rain, earthquakes, undercutting, or human activity

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Factors affecting slope stability: angle, geology (weak layers, joints), water content (lubricates and adds weight), vegetation (stabilises or destabilises)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Subsidence: ground sinking due to dissolution of limestone (sinkholes), mining, or groundwater extraction

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Monitoring: satellite (InSAR), GPS, strain gauges, seismometers, gas monitoring, groundwater level sensors

cards.front: Recall a key point about Geological Hazard Processes
cards.back: Management: hazard mapping, building codes, slope stabilisation, drainage, early warning systems, evacuation planning

cards.front: What should you know about gcse geology exam tips — geological hazard processes?
cards.back: 1. For Geological Hazard Processes questions, use correct geological terminology and classify features precisely 2. Reference specific geological time periods and processes 3. When interpreting data, consider the quality and limitations of the evidence 4. Apply your understanding of Geological Hazard Processes to fieldwork observations and map data 5. For evaluation, weigh competing geological theories with evidence
Explain the causes of landslides and describe how geological hazard risk can be monitored and managed. [6 marks]

AO1 (Knowledge & Understanding): Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of geological hazard processes, including key geological concepts, observational data and theoretical models relevant to OCR J357. AO2 (Application of Knowledge): Apply knowledge and understanding of geological hazard processes to both familiar and unfamiliar geological contexts, using field evidence and theoretical principle
